therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Type 2 diabetes mellitus patients inadequately controlled on metformin or sulfonylurea monotherapy
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Composite of cardiovascular death and cardiovascular hospitalisation events

results.target_engagement_evidence: Improved insulin sensitivity (HOMA: +42.57% RSG+MET vs -3.45% SU+MET), reduced fasting plasma glucose, reduced HbA1c, reduced free fatty acids, reduced CRP
biomarker_changes: HbA1c change at Month 60: RSG+MET -0.14%, SU+MET +0.17%, RSG+SU -0.24%, MET+SU -0.10%
Fasting plasma glucose change at Month 60: RSG+MET -1.38 mmol/L, SU+MET -0.29 mmol/L, RSG+SU -2.00 mmol/L, MET+SU -0.94 mmol/L
Insulin sensitivity (HOMA) at Month 60: RSG+MET +42.57%, SU+MET -3.45%, RSG+SU +42.07%, MET+SU +23.90%
Beta cell function (HOMA) at Month 60: RSG+MET +20.54%, SU+MET +19.28%, RSG+SU +32.35%, MET+SU +12.43%
HDL-cholesterol at Month 60: RSG+MET +9.95%, SU+MET +2.57%, RSG+SU +7.73%, MET+SU +6.14%
LDL-cholesterol at Month 60: RSG+MET -12.70%, SU+MET -17.68%, RSG+SU -8.99%, MET+SU -17.80%
CRP at Month 60: RSG+MET -57.40%, SU+MET -28.92%, RSG+SU -56.50%, MET+SU -36.29%
Body weight change at Month 60: RSG+MET +3.93 kg, SU+MET -0.54 kg, RSG+SU +4.72 kg, MET+SU -2.16 kg
Waist circumference change at Month 60: RSG+MET +2.70 cm, SU+MET +0.65 cm, RSG+SU +3.00 cm, MET+SU -0.60 cm
PAI-1 antigen at Month 60: RSG+MET -9.85%, SU+MET +15.01%, RSG+SU -7.79%, MET+SU -0.64%
Free fatty acids at Month 60: RSG+MET -16.46%, SU+MET +2.79%, RSG+SU -11.58%, MET+SU +4.47%
subgroup_findings: CHF (fatal or non-fatal): RSG 61 vs MET/SU 29 — higher in rosiglitazone group
Hospitalisation for congestive heart failure: RSG 69 vs MET/SU 36 — higher in rosiglitazone group
Stroke (fatal or non-fatal): RSG 46 vs MET/SU 63 — lower in rosiglitazone group (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.54–1.14)
Acute MI (fatal or non-fatal): RSG 64 vs MET/SU 56 — numerically higher in rosiglitazone group (HR 1.13, 95% CI 0.80–1.59)
All-cause death: RSG 136 vs MET/SU 157 (HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.68–1.08)
Bone fractures overall (main study + OFU): RSG 238 vs MET/SU 151 — higher in rosiglitazone group
Bone fractures in females (main study + OFU): RSG 156 vs MET/SU 91 — markedly higher in rosiglitazone group
Glycaemic failure: RSG+MET 281 vs SU+MET 451; RSG+SU 365 vs MET+SU 424 — fewer failures with rosiglitazone
Insulin initiation: RSG+MET 126 vs SU+MET 276; RSG+SU 168 vs MET+SU 259 — fewer insulin starts with rosiglitazone
safety_signals: Increased risk of congestive heart failure with rosiglitazone (61 vs 29 fatal/non-fatal CHF events)
Increased bone fractures with rosiglitazone, particularly in women (156 vs 91 female fractures over main study + OFU)
Numerically higher MI rate with rosiglitazone (HR 1.13–1.15 across adjudication definitions, CIs crossing 1.0)
Weight gain with rosiglitazone: +3.93 kg (RSG+MET) and +4.72 kg (RSG+SU) vs weight loss/stability in comparators
Increased waist circumference with rosiglitazone vs comparators

context.comparator: Sulfonylurea added to metformin or metformin added to sulfonylurea (active comparator)
context.duration: Up to 7.5 years (main study); up to 11.4 years including observational follow-up

modulation_entries.hypothesis: Rosiglitazone improves peripheral insulin sensitivity via PPAR-gamma agonism, complementing metformin's hepatic glucose output suppression to produce additive glycaemic control and greater insulin sensitivity improvement than either agent alone
modulation_entries.citation: Insulin sensitivity (HOMA) at Month 60: RSG+MET +42.57% vs SU+MET -3.45%; RSG+MET showed greater HbA1c reduction (-0.14%) and FPG reduction (-1.38 mmol/L) compared to SU+MET (+0.17%, -0.29 mmol/L)

modulation_entries.hypothesis: Rosiglitazone improves peripheral insulin sensitivity, augmenting the glycaemic effect of sulfonylurea-stimulated insulin secretion and reducing insulin resistance that limits sulfonylurea efficacy
modulation_entries.citation: Insulin sensitivity (HOMA) at Month 60: RSG+SU +42.07% vs MET+SU +23.90%; RSG+SU showed greater HbA1c reduction (-0.24%) and FPG reduction (-2.00 mmol/L) compared to MET+SU (-0.10%, -0.94 mmol/L)
